\[
\log_6(x-y)+\log_6(x+y)=2
\]

Using log rules:

\[
\log_6\big((x-y)(x+y)\big)=2
\]

\[
(x-y)(x+y)=6^2=36
\]

\[
x^2-y^2=36
\]

Also,

\[
\log_y(5x)=2
\]

so

\[
5x=y^2
\]

Substitute into \(x^2-y^2=36\):

\[
x^2-5x=36
\]

\[
x^2-5x-36=0
\]

\[
(x-9)(x+4)=0
\]

Thus,

\[
x=9 \quad \text{or} \quad x=-4
\]

Since \(\log_y(5x)\) requires \(5x>0\), we need \(x>0\). Therefore,

\[
\boxed{9}
\]
